correctness.rationale: For an initially stationary heading, the reset generator gives harmonics E cos(jΘ)=r/(r+j²d), E sin(jΘ)=0. Both centered velocity harmonics decay at rate λ=r+d; stationarity and independence of the translational Brownian motion justify integrating the angular covariance kernel and adding 2Dt. Reflection makes the off-diagonal covariance vanish. The ratio of the lag weights (t₂−s)/(t₁−s) increases strictly on shared support, with additional support to the right for the longer lag. Normalizing therefore strictly increases the mean of s, making the derivative of the log variance ratio strictly negative. The zero-rate limit is the squared time ratio; the large-rate limit follows from Hλ(t)∼t/λ. The transverse amplitude at fixed u,λ is proportional to g(z)=(1+z)²/[z²(4+z)]; its log derivative is strictly negative and its limits are infinity and zero, proving sufficiency and uniqueness for positive parameters. At z=2/13 and 1/4 the excess anisotropy equals 26/25, and the positive rates exist uniquely because 6/325 and 17/400 both lie in (0,1/2), the range of Hλ(1). Adding 2 to both excess variances gives the stated covariance. This is exact ensemble identifiability with known D and reset direction, not a conditioning theorem or an ambiguity of full displacement laws.
